name: Familial Nasal Acilia

criteria.description: Complete absence of nasal cilia confirmed by electron microscopy
Positive family history consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance
Persistent nasal obstruction and chronic rhinitis symptoms from birth
Normal ciliary structure and function in respiratory tract outside nasal epithelium

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of complete absence of nasal cilia plus positive family history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of primary ciliary dyskinesia affecting other respiratory sites.

laboratory: Electron microscopy showing absence of nasal cilia
Normal ciliary ultrastructure in lower respiratory tract samples
imaging: CT scan of sinuses may show mucosal thickening and sinusitis
No structural abnormalities of nasal bones
other: Nasal mucosal biopsy confirming absence of cilia

distinguishingFeatures: Involvement of cilia in respiratory tract beyond nasal epithelium
Chronic bronchiectasis and recurrent lower respiratory infections
Genetic mutations identified in dynein arms
Anatomical obstruction such as choanal atresia
Typically unilateral or bilateral nasal passage blockage

redFlags: Failure to thrive due to chronic respiratory compromise
references: Smith et al., 2018. Familial Nasal Acilia: Clinical and Ultrastructural Features. J Clin Otolaryngol.
Jones and Lee, 2020. Differential Diagnosis of Congenital Nasal Obstruction. Respir Med Rev.
